prompt.context: Deloitte has been asked to help Coffee, a large multinational women's clothing retailer with worldwide revenues of over $3B in 2011. Coffee sells sports, formal, and casual apparel. Despite strong overall performance, its American operation has an underperforming brand under review with some associated stores already closed. The American operation has two major umbrella brands: 'Coffee' (formal wear) and 'Tea' (casual wear). Channels and 2011 revenues are: Coffee branded retail stores $200M; Tea branded retail stores $20M; Coffee branded outlet stores $150M; Wholesale to major chains (e.g., Macy's) $600M. Tea has historically been neglected but has consistently generated profit with minimal management attention and capital reinvestment. Coffee wants to understand whether divesting Tea and refocusing on its core Coffee brand is better, or whether holding Tea and milking it as a cash cow is preferable.
prompt.question: Deloitte has been approached by Coffee to assess whether Coffee should hold or sell the Tea brand. Please address the following: (1) Using the terms of the sale from the data sheet, find the revenues for 2012 that the buyer would receive from buying Tea, and the revenues Coffee could maintain by not selling Tea. (2) How would you value the sell scenario and the hold scenario? (3) If Coffee holds Tea, how long will it take for Tea's cash flow to equal the $50M sale price? (4) What do you recommend Coffee do? (5) Are there any other relevant issues that may affect the valuation or divestment decision?

clarifying_info.q: What exactly is included in the sale of Tea?
clarifying_info.a: The sale of Tea includes only Tea's branded product sales in Tea's retail channel and Tea's wholesale business. The buyer will not have access to Coffee's outlet stores or Coffee branded retail stores for distribution.

clarifying_info.q: How many Tea retail stores will be open at the start of 2012?
clarifying_info.a: 20 Tea branded stores will be open at the start of 2012 (down from 32 at the start of 2011).

clarifying_info.q: How many Coffee retail stores will be open at the start of 2012?
clarifying_info.a: 150 Coffee branded stores will be open at the start of 2012 (up from 125 at the start of 2011).

clarifying_info.q: Are wholesale sales expected to change in 2012?
clarifying_info.a: No, sales in the wholesale channel are expected to remain unchanged in CY2012.

clarifying_info.q: What tax rate should I use for the payback calculation?
clarifying_info.a: You may assume a 40% tax rate if you want to refine to after-tax cash flow.

exhibits.title: Data Sheet – Store Counts, Revenue Multiples, General Info, Tea Brand Historical Performance, Brand vs. Channel Sales CY2011
exhibits.shows: A data sheet with four sections: (1) Number of Retail Stores table showing Coffee branded stores (100/125/150) and Tea branded stores (45/32/20) at start of 2010/2011/2012; (2) Revenue Multiples for Consumer Product Transactions in the U.S. – five comparable transactions with revenue multiple, deal size ($M), and date; (3) General Information with terms of sale bullet points; (4) Tea Brand Business Historical Performance (% of sales) for 2009-2011 showing Revenues, Gross Profit, EBIT, SG&A, COGS; (5) Brand vs. Channel Sales CY2011 ($M) matrix showing Coffee Brand products and Tea Brand products across Coffee branded retail stores, Tea branded retail stores, Coffee branded outlets, and Wholesale
exhibits.data: Store counts – Coffee stores: 100/125/150; Tea stores: 45/32/20. Comparable transactions: A: 0.6x, $147M, Jan 2011; B: 0.7x, $300M, Mar 2011; C: 0.9x, $180M, Apr 2010; D: 0.6x, $70M, Oct 2010; E: 1.9x, $5M, Nov 2007. Tea Brand historical margins – EBIT: 12%/11%/10% (2009/2010/2011); COGS: 77%/77%/78%; SG&A: 5%/6%/6%; Gross Profit: 23%/23%/22%. Brand vs. Channel CY2011 ($M) – Coffee Brand: retail stores 180, Tea stores 10, outlets 120, wholesale 540; Tea Brand: Coffee retail stores 20, Tea stores 10, outlets 30, wholesale 60.

framework: Define scope of sell vs. hold: isolate which revenues transfer with Tea vs. those retained by Coffee
Project 2012 revenues for each scenario by scaling store counts and applying channel assumptions
Value each scenario using revenue multiples from comparable transactions (with outlier adjustment)
Calculate payback period if Coffee holds (sale price / annual cash flow from Tea)
Make a recommendation comparing hold value vs. sell value
Identify qualitative risks and other considerations (strategy fit, stranded costs, buyer types, transaction costs)

questions.prompt: Q1a: What are the 2012 revenues the buyer would receive from buying Tea (sell scenario)?
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply the terms of sale: buyer only gets Tea retail channel and Tea wholesale. Tea retail revenue must be scaled by store openings at start of 2012 vs. 2011 (20/32 = 0.625). Wholesale is unchanged at $60M.

math.setup: From CY2011 Brand vs. Channel matrix, Tea branded products sold through Tea retail stores = $10M; Tea wholesale = $60M. Stores: 20 open at start of 2012 vs. 32 at start of 2011, so scaling factor = 20/32 = 0.625.

questions.prompt: Q1b: What are the 2012 revenues Coffee could maintain by holding Tea (hold scenario)?
questions.guidance: Candidate must include ALL channels through which Tea branded products are sold when held: Tea retail stores (scaled down), Coffee retail stores (Tea products sold there, scaled up), Coffee outlets (Tea products remain), and wholesale. Must scale Coffee retail by 150/125 = 1.2 and Tea retail by 20/32 = 0.625.

math.setup: From CY2011 matrix: Tea products in Coffee retail = $20M; Tea products in Tea stores = $10M; Tea products in outlets = $30M; Tea wholesale = $60M. Coffee stores: 150/125 = 1.2 scale-up. Tea stores: 20/32 = 0.625 scale-down. Outlets and wholesale unchanged.

questions.prompt: Q2: How would you value the sell scenario and the hold scenario using the comparable transactions?
questions.guidance: Good answer applies the unadjusted average multiple (0.9x) to both revenue bases. Better answer removes Transaction E (1.9x, Nov 2007) as dated/pre-crash and uses the adjusted average (0.7x). Great answer also discusses qualitative factors that could affect buyer willingness to pay premium or discount (dormant demand, store leases, Coffee's ability to replace lost revenues, ROI comparison for hold scenario).

math.setup: Sell scenario revenues = $66.25M; Hold scenario revenues = $120.25M. Revenue multiples – five comps; unadjusted average = (0.6+0.7+0.9+0.6+1.9)/5 = 4.7/5 = 0.94 ≈ 0.9. Adjusted (remove Transaction E as pre-crash outlier from 2007): (0.6+0.7+0.9+0.6)/4 = 2.8/4 = 0.7.
math.answer: Sell ≈ $46M–$60M; Hold ≈ $84M–$108M (better answer uses adjusted 0.7x: Sell ~$46M, Hold ~$84M)

questions.prompt: Q3: If Coffee holds Tea, how long will it take for Tea's cash flow to equal the $50M hypothetical sale price?
questions.guidance: Good answer uses EBIT margin (10%) on hold revenues to get $12M/year, yielding ~4+ year payback. Better answer adjusts for taxes (40% rate) to get after-tax earnings of 6% × $120.25M ≈ $7.2M/year, yielding ~7 year payback. Candidate should note EBIT is not true cash flow.

math.setup: Hold revenues = $120.25M. EBIT margin (2011) = 10%. Tax rate = 40% (if adjusted). Sale price = $50M (given). Ignore time value of money.
steps: Good answer – pre-tax: Annual EBIT = 10% × $120.25M ≈ $12M; Payback = $50M / $12M ≈ 4.2 years
Better answer – after-tax: Net income margin = 10% × (1 – 40%) = 6%; Annual net income = 6% × $120.25M ≈ $7.2M; Payback = $50M / $7.2M ≈ 6.9 years
math.answer: ~4 years (pre-tax EBIT basis) or ~7 years (after-tax basis)

questions.prompt: Q4: What do you recommend Coffee do?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare hold value (~$84M) to sell value (~$46M) and recommend holding. At minimum they should recommend the higher-value scenario. Strong answers include additional strategic actions for the hold case and acknowledge declining Tea retail trends and EBIT margin erosion.

questions.prompt: Q5: What other issues may affect the valuation or divestment decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover several categories: overall strategy fit (does Tea fit Coffee's vision?); ability to change (can Coffee halt Tea's slide?); impact on remaining revenue streams post-divestiture; potential buyer types and issues (PE vs. strategic buyer); transaction costs (banker fees, management distraction); stranded costs (shared services between brands).

brainstorming.prompt: What other relevant issues may affect the valuation or the divestment decision?

categories.name: Strategic Fit
ideas: Does Tea's brand positioning, product mix, and styling align with Coffee's overall women's apparel strategy?
Could Tea be used to extend Coffee's addressable market into casual wear at scale?

categories.name: Ability to Turn Around Tea
ideas: Does Coffee management have appetite and capacity to implement changes needed to halt Tea's decline?
Potential actions: open more Tea stores, enterprise cost reduction, international expansion, broader wholesale distribution

categories.name: Impact on Remaining Business
ideas: Revenue streams lost from Tea products sold through Coffee retail stores and outlets
Risk of stranded overhead costs when Tea is carved out
Impact on wholesale relationships if Tea is removed from the portfolio

categories.name: Potential Buyers
ideas: Private equity: carve-out experience but unlikely to overpay; would need to build standalone back office if no similar portfolio companies
Strategic buyer: may take brand up- or down-market; existing retailer may close remaining Tea stores; lack of back office complicates bolt-on deals

categories.name: Transaction Costs and Complexity
ideas: Banker fees and advisory costs reduce net sale proceeds
Management distraction during deal process hurts core Coffee business
Timing risk: the longer the process, the more Tea stores close and the lower the eventual sale price

categories.name: Stranded Costs
ideas: Shared services (IT, HR, logistics, marketing) across Coffee and Tea brands
Post-sale, Coffee bears these costs alone without Tea's revenue contribution

recommendation: Recommend Coffee hold the Tea brand, as its value to Coffee in the hold scenario (~$84M at 0.7x) exceeds the sell scenario (~$46M at 0.7x)
If Coffee holds Tea, it should actively invest to stabilize and grow the brand rather than passively milking it
risks: Tea's EBIT margin has been declining (12% in 2009 to 10% in 2011) and Tea retail stores continue to shrink — inaction will erode value further
If Coffee lacks management bandwidth or appetite for change, holding Tea may simply delay an inevitable lower-value sale
next_steps: Assess strategic options to revitalize Tea: expand Tea retail stores, broaden wholesale distribution, consider international rollout
Conduct cost-structure review to identify enterprise cost reduction opportunities in Tea
Monitor Tea's EBIT trajectory and set a clear performance threshold — if margin drops below X%, trigger a formal sale process
Evaluate potential back-office shared services that must be ring-fenced if sale is eventually pursued
